Publish.LongDescription:
⚠️ **This is the development build of _Traffic: Clear the Way_. It is not the mod you want.**
Install the normal release instead - this page exists so testers can try changes before they ship.
- Expect rough edges: unfinished behaviour, debug logging, values that change between uploads. - Do **not** run it on a city you care about. Keep a backup save. - Never run it alongside the release version - both register the same systems.
Feedback on a dev build is most useful with `Logs/ClearTheWay.log` attached (switch on "Verbose logging" in the options first).
Release version: https://mods.paradoxplaza.com/mods/151583/Windows
Publish.ChangeLog:
0.1.13.3 - a performance measurement you can switch on in the options.
Behaviour is unchanged from 0.1.13.2. This build is for measuring frame cost in your own city.
**New: Performance tab in the mod options** - "All on" / "All off" switch every part of the mod at once. Measuring everything is good for an overview, and the most expensive setting. - "Show single passes" opens the list of single switches, one per part (main corridor pass, second pass, path-end guard, pedestrian hold, escalation chain, corridor builder, lane change, pulling cars aside, oncoming-lane logic, arrival assist, accident pass, recovery assist, tow coupling). Measure one at a time for clean numbers. - Every 300 simulation frames the mod writes [perf] lines to Logs/ClearTheWay.log: total time, number of calls, average and worst call, and the cost per tick. - Switches take effect on the next tick, no restart. Every change is written to the log with its frame, so a log can be split there and the two halves compared. - All switches are off by default and cost nothing while off. Leave them off for normal play.
**Log format** - Numbers in Logs/ClearTheWay.log are now always written with a decimal point ("speed=69.4", "total=0.28ms"), whatever language the game runs in. On a German or French system they used to come out with a decimal comma, so logs from different players did not read the same.
**What to report** Your ClearTheWay.log with one switch on (or "All on"), the city size, and roughly how many emergency vehicles and wrecks were on the map.
